key_insight: VideoNet introduces a large-scale, domain-focused video dataset and benchmark that restores rigorous evaluation of action recognition—revealing that current vision-language models struggle with fine-grained, temporally extended, domain-specific actions.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of diverse, challenging, domain-specific video data and standardized benchmarks for evaluating action recognition capabilities in modern vision-language models and action-recognition systems.
method: Curate and annotate a large-scale collection of videos emphasizing domain-specific, temporally extended actions (e.g., specialized workflows, sports maneuvers, procedural tasks).
Design standardized evaluation protocols and benchmark splits to evaluate both VLMs and dedicated action-recognition models on fine-grained temporal labels.
Provide baseline evaluations and analysis to quantify current model gaps and guide future model development.
impact: Enables researchers and practitioners to benchmark temporal and domain-specific action understanding reliably, driving development of models that better handle real-world, multi-frame actions and specialized applications.

paper_title: VideoNet: A Large-Scale Dataset for Domain-Specific Action Recognition
paper_authors: Tanush Yadav, Mohammadreza Salehi, Jae Sung Park, Vivek Ramanujan, Hannaneh Hajishirzi
